turns.doctor_question: Hello. What brings you in to see me today?
turns.patient_response: Well, um... I guess it's because work has just been really hard lately. I'm a hairstylist, and lately, my hands feel like they’re moving through glue at work. Like, even just sectioning hair or mixing color takes me forever now. People have started noticing I’m just slower than I used to be. My manager actually pulled me aside the other day to ask if I was feeling okay, which was super embarrassing because we were right by the breakroom and I think Jessica heard us. Jessica is this other stylist who always tries to take my walk-ins, and she’s been side-eyeing me a lot lately. I swear she’s just waiting for me to mess up so she can steal my clients. She always wears these really loud, chunky bracelets that clink against the chair when she's cutting, and it's so distracting, you know? But yeah, I just... I can't seem to move as fast as I need to.

turns.doctor_question: Alongside feeling physically slowed down like this, how has your overall mood been lately?
turns.patient_response: My mood? Um... it's just bad. Most days I wake up with this really heavy, flat sadness right in my chest. It just sits there, you know? It makes me feel like... like there’s just no point in trying to build the life I was planning. I had this whole plan to open my own salon suite by the time I turned 23. I even had a Pinterest board for it and everything. I wanted to paint the walls this really specific shade of sage green, because green is supposed to be super calming. Which is kind of funny, actually, because my aunt had a green kitchen and she was the most high-strung person I've ever met. She had this tiny white poodle named Barnaby that would just yap and yap all day long while she was cooking. She used to make this amazing baked ziti, though. I haven't had baked ziti in forever. I should probably try to make it, but the good mozzarella is always so expensive at the grocery store near my apartment, and the lines there are always ridiculous on Tuesdays... wait, what did you ask me? Oh, right. Yeah, my mood is just really sad and heavy.

turns.doctor_question: Have you ever heard voices, whispers, or other sounds when no one else was around or that other people couldn't hear?
turns.patient_response:
Um, yeah... actually, I do. Sometimes when I’m sweeping up hair or rinsing out the color bowls in the back, I hear this woman’s voice. It always sounds like it's coming from right near the shampoo stations, and she just keeps saying that I’m ruining everything. And it happens even when the salon is completely empty or when I know for a fact nobody is anywhere near me. 

But honestly, those shampoo stations are just a nightmare anyway. We have these deep black ceramic bowls, and they show every single water spot. My manager makes us use this weird organic cleaner on them, and it smells exactly like black licorice, which is so gross. I used to love black licorice when I was little, though. My grandpa always kept a jar of Good & Plenty candies on his coffee table. He had this massive, old leather couch that would completely stick to your legs in the summer if you were wearing shorts. I used to try to sit on a throw blanket so I wouldn't peel my skin off when I stood up... but wait, what was I talking about? Oh, right, the voice. Yeah, it just tells me I'm ruining things.

symptom_reasoning.S020: The patient explicitly confirms hearing a woman's voice telling her she is ruining everything when the salon is empty and no one is around.
symptom_reasoning.S021: The patient exhibits tangential speech and derailment, drifting from the topic of the voice to shampoo bowls, organic cleaner, black licorice, her grandfather's candies, and his leather couch before losing her train of thought.

turns.doctor_question: Looking back over the entire time since you first started hearing that voice, would you say you have felt this deep sadness for most of that time, or only a small part of it?
turns.patient_response: Um, looking back... I'd say I've spent most of this whole time feeling depressed and weighed down. Like, almost the entire time since this all started. I actually tried to keep track of how I was feeling in my planner for a while. I buy a new one every single January. I usually get the ones from Target with the thick spiral binding because they lay flat on the breakroom table. Last year I got this beautiful one with a floral print on the cover, but the gold foil started peeling off by like, March. It drove me crazy. I hate when things look cheap, you know? My mom always says you get what you pay for, which is why she refuses to buy shoes anywhere except big department stores. She has this one pair of brown leather loafers that she’s literally worn since 2018. They look so stiff and uncomfortable, though, and they have this weird little tassel on the front that flops around when she walks. I keep telling her to just buy some comfortable sneakers, but she says sneakers aren't professional... wait, sorry, I lost my train of thought again. What did you ask me? Oh, right. Yeah, looking back, I've spent most of this whole decline feeling really depressed and weighed down, with only a few shorter stretches where the sadness wasn't as prominent.
